prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by chemically induced proximity, through heterobifunctional degraders that recruit an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a chosen protein and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B055 to B019. After round 1, my own case for Gray and Winkler stands as good science with the cleanest attribution, but it did not attract support from any other member, and three colleagues (Aqvist, Chabes, Sparr) independently raised the 1992 Marcus prize as covering its conceptual core. I cannot show the committee, from what is on the table, that the protein experiments are a distinct discovery rather than the experimental half of a recognised one. B019 rests on a mechanism I can state in physical terms: a small molecule imposes a neo-interaction that forms a ternary complex between an E3 ligase and a target, and the chemistry of the complex (ligand, linker, cooperativity) decides whether the protein is removed. That is supported by ternary-complex structures and by reproduction in many independent laboratories. The three-name configuration Crews, Deshaies and Handa also answers the objection I raised in round 1, that Handa's identification of cereblon is a distinct and mechanistic discovery that explains a marketed drug class. Crews and Deshaies give the concept and first demonstrations, Handa gives the molecular basis of the glue strand, and the common logic is E3 ligase hijacking, so a single citation can be written without overstating either strand.
statement.case_against: My reservations on B019 remain and I do not withdraw them. Clinical validation is incomplete: as far as any member has stated, and I cannot verify this from the files, no degrader is approved, so the award would rest on concept and mechanism. PROTACs and cereblon-mediated glues have different histories, and a three-person cap leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim, whose claims are real. Sakamoto's first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies is a priority point that I cannot settle without the expert reports. The citation has to be written carefully so that it does not read as crediting Handa with PROTAC design, or Crews and Deshaies with the cereblon discovery. The ternary-complex cooperativity biophysics is still only partly quantified, which weakens the claim that the design is fully rational. Finally, my move toward the broadest-supported ballot must not be read as counting votes: I changed because B055 has an unresolved overlap with a prior prize and no support, not because B019 has five explicit supporters.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers Ciulli as the third laureate with a PROTAC-only citation, arguing that rational ligand and structural design is the connection between mechanism and experiment, and that the Nobel standard is a concept with demonstrated consequences, not a marketed drug.
responses.response: I accept your point on approval: the standard is a demonstrated new concept, and degraders meet it. I still prefer Handa to Ciulli. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are an important refinement of a concept that Crews and Deshaies had already established, whereas the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a separate mechanistic discovery that explains why a drug class works. A PROTAC-only citation also leaves unexplained the strand that has the clearest clinical record. If the committee wants a narrower PROTAC prize, I would need the expert reports to show that the glue strand is derivative, and nothing so far indicates that. Your Ciulli configuration is my first fallback if the committee splits on this.

responses.point: Chabes asked what the field reports say about Handa versus Ciulli, and he supports a citation that joins heterobifunctional PROTACs and cereblon as the glue target; he also notes the early Crews and Deshaies PROTAC used a poorly permeable peptide ligand.
responses.response: Your reasoning moved me. I asked in round 1 for evidence about Handa versus Ciulli and I have still not seen the reports, but your account of cereblon as the molecular explanation behind thalidomide is the kind of mechanism I weigh most. I also agree with your point on the first PROTAC being proof of concept: that is why I would write the citation around the induced-proximity principle and not around drug-like PROTACs as a finished modality. On B046 we agree that the cofactor structures are secure but the N2 reduction mechanism is not, which is why I keep it only as an alternative.

responses.point: Somfai asks what is chemically new in degraders and prefers Ciulli to a mixed PROTAC-plus-glue trio, while expecting a PROTAC-only citation to draw the Handa objection; he prefers B034, citing three decades of confirmation.
responses.response: On chemical novelty I side with Aili and Zou: the new thing is not a reaction but a design principle, a bifunctional or glue-like molecule creating a neo-interaction so that a protein is removed instead of blocked, and the chemistry lies in controlling that ternary complex. On B034, I respect the three decades of confirmation and the compact attribution, but a C-N coupling extends the cross-coupling idea recognised in 2010, and Kosugi and Migita are an unresolved precursor, so I do not see it overcoming that objection better than my own B055 overcame the Marcus one. I agree with you that the mixed trio is a compromise, and I think it is better to be explicit about that in the citation.

responses.point: The chair asks whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one achievement or two, whether the lack of an approved degrader is a reason to defer, and what a three-name B019 defence needs; he also corrects his earlier overstatement of opening support.
responses.response: Thank you for the correction on the opening ranks, since I was one of the two who ranked B019 low. On your first question, I think it is one achievement in logic and two in history: the shared principle is recruitment of an E3 ligase to a protein that it would not normally degrade, with cereblon showing that the same logic was operating in a drug used for decades. A two-part prize is blocked by the three-person cap, so a single citation naming the principle is the honest option. On deferral, I would accept evidence of a degrader validated in late-stage trials, but I do not make approval a precondition. My remaining concern is maturity of the cooperativity biophysics, and I would not defer a mechanism that is already well reproduced.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts PROTACs and cereblon-mediated glues as one achievement with one citation, or whether a Ciulli-based PROTAC-only configuration is the more defensible one.
Priority of Sakamoto's first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies, and the relative weight of Ito, Gray and Kim on the glue strand, which I cannot settle without the expert reports.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader, which I could not verify from the files, should still count against recognition this year.
Whether the 1992 Marcus prize truly covers B055, which I now treat as an unresolved question and not as a reason to prefer it.
Whether my Round 1 B055 preference was influenced by my own research in proton and electron transfer, which I now discount.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional conflict with any of the B019 candidates (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) or with the alternatives is apparent from my profile. In round 1 I disclosed that my research on proton and electron transfer in cytochrome c oxidase is scientifically close to B055; it is no longer in my preferred configuration, but it remains an alternative and my bias toward that field should still be weighed. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, which has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate.
